newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING to stay in U.S. general insurance.
newsitem.headline: ING to stay in U.S. general insurance.

text.p: Financial services group ING Groep NV (ING) said on Tuesday it would hold on to its general insurance activities in the United States.
Executive board chairman Aad Jacobs told a news conference ING had found it difficult for several years to reach its target return on equity of 11 percent from these activities.
But he said ING expected this goal to be achieved in 1997, representing a profit of about $44 million on the capital employed of $400 million.
"I think we will hold on to it because it's developing more favourably," he said.
Jacobs had been asked if ING would sell these operations.
Some analysts have speculated the Dutch group would sell its U.S. non-life activities to focus on expansion in life insurance.
Setbacks such as severe winters and natural disasters have plagued these operations.
ING earlier announced it had agreed to buy Equitable of Iowa for $2.2 billion in shares and cash.
